findings.title: Cleanup loses the process group of an already successful compiler driver.
findings.trigger: A compiler driver starts a child and exits successfully; a later compiler in the batch fails or the build is interrupted.
findings.cause: join_jobs drops each successful driver PID from PIDS at line 60. stop_jobs only signals groups represented by the remaining PIDS. The successful driver group can still contain active descendants.
findings.observed: Pinned Linux fake-tool fixture: src/a.c driver PID/process group 15 exited successfully; child PID 18 remained active in state S and group 15 after src/b.c failed, the build returned 1, and ctlbuild scratch was deleted. macOS also reproduced an active surviving child.
findings.impact: Owned compiler descendants can survive a failed invocation and continue after their scratch directory is removed. This violates the requested cleanup contract. Existing seven suites remain valid for their covered cases but miss this ordering.
findings.probe_cleanup: The probe sent SIGKILL only to its recorded child PIDs and verified they were absent or stopped (Linux zombie state Z). No shared process was signalled.
findings.repair_recommendation: In a fresh stage2, preserve cleanup ownership for residual compiler process groups after their direct drivers have been joined, or stop residual descendants before dropping group tracking. Add a regression for earlier successful driver plus later failure, and the related interruption case. Keep compile flags, source/object order, link and image checks unchanged.
findings.disposition: Material failure reported to root. No repair was made. Do not advance to stage4.

Compiler CF string and complete L=$B/lib onward link/post-link block are byte-equal to the audit base. Source glob, object basename construction and link append order remain. Deterministic diagnostic collection uses source-unit order.

Controller reuse file matches the exact built/current script hashes and exact unified diff. Only failure/signal cleanup changed after the real successful build. Reusing its successful build/image result remains justified; the newly found cleanup defect does not invalidate successful output equivalence.
No diff exists in tests/run_tests.sh, active build/validator helper sources or BUILDING.md. Their owners retain control.
